decisions.decision: How should predictions be served on production devices?
decisions.context: Cameras need local inference because production lines often lack network access.

alternatives.label: Local service/API based model serving
pros: Low latency: avoids network round trips
cons: Tight budget: adds local service management

alternatives.label: Microservice based model serving
cons: Offline operation: depends on reachable service
Tight budget: adds service infrastructure

decisions.rationale: Offline operation decides the choice: local serving keeps inference available without network access. This gives up the separation of a distributed service. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:5 and v:5.2.
consequences: Inference runs on each device.
Device resources must support serving.
Network outages do not block predictions.

decisions.decision: How should the model integrate with the camera application?
decisions.context: The model must run alongside the inspection application on devices with intermittent connectivity.

alternatives.label: Model in monolith
pros: Offline operation: model ships with application
cons: Maintainability: model and app release together

alternatives.label: Model as a service
cons: Offline operation: service must be available locally or remotely
Tight budget: adds service deployment

decisions.rationale: Offline operation decides the choice: embedding the model keeps application inference self-contained. This gives up independent model-service releases. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:1 and v:1.2.
consequences: The application package includes the model.
App and model updates are coupled.
Local deployment stays simple.

decisions.decision: How should weekly retraining be triggered?
decisions.context: Newly labelled images arrive for regular retraining, so training should run on a predictable cadence.

alternatives.label: On-schedule trigger
pros: Weekly updates: matches a regular cadence
cons: Tight budget: scheduled runs may occur without new labels

alternatives.label: On-demand trigger
pros: Tight budget: run only when requested
cons: Weekly updates: requires manual action
Reproducibility: timing can vary

decisions.rationale: Weekly updates decide the choice: scheduled runs match the stated retraining cadence. This gives up avoiding runs when no new labels are available. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:12 and v:12.3.
consequences: A scheduler starts weekly training.
Training data availability needs checking.
Runs are easy to anticipate.

decisions.decision: How should the model be trained?
decisions.context: The brief specifies weekly retraining from newly labelled images rather than continuous adaptation on the production device.

alternatives.label: Batch-based learning
pros: Reproducibility: trains from a fixed batch
cons: Freshness: labels wait for the next run

alternatives.label: Incremental learning
cons: Reproducibility: model evolves across updates
Tight budget: may add operational complexity

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice: each weekly run can train from a fixed image set. This gives up incorporating labels immediately. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:19 and v:19.1.
consequences: Each run produces a discrete model artifact.
Training can run away from production devices.
Dataset selection must be recorded.

decisions.decision: How should training data be versioned?
decisions.context: Weekly training must be repeatable against specific newly labelled image sets.

alternatives.label: Data version repository
pros: Weekly updates: tracks successive image sets
cons: Tight budget: adds repository tooling and storage

alternatives.label: No data versioning
cons: Reproducibility: cannot reliably identify training set

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice: versioned data makes weekly training inputs identifiable. This gives up some simplicity and storage budget. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:11 and v:11.1.
consequences: Each model release links to a dataset version.
Versioned images consume storage.
Training runs can be traced to inputs.

decisions.decision: How should models be delivered to devices?
decisions.context: A small team must push weekly model updates to production devices.

alternatives.label: CI/CD pipeline
cons: Tight budget: requires pipeline setup and upkeep

alternatives.label: Build and Deployment scripts
cons: Weekly updates: manual execution adds effort
Reproducibility: steps can drift

decisions.rationale: Weekly updates decide the choice: a pipeline reduces repeated delivery work for the small team. This gives up the lower initial setup cost of scripts. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:8 and v:8.1.
consequences: Deployment steps are automated.
Pipeline maintenance is required.
Device connectivity and update windows need coordination.

decisions.decision: What should be tested before model release?
decisions.context: A newly trained model is pushed to production each week, making a quality gate important before deployment.

alternatives.label: Testing trained model quality
pros: Reproducibility: applies a quality gate to each model
Weekly updates: checks every trained release
cons: Tight budget: requires labelled evaluation data and compute

alternatives.label: No testing
cons: Weekly updates: defects can ship with each release
Reproducibility: no consistent quality gate

decisions.rationale: Weekly updates decide the choice: test every trained model before it reaches devices. This gives up some compute and evaluation-data budget. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:26 and v:26.9.
consequences: Each release requires an evaluation set.
Quality thresholds must be defined.
Failed candidates need a release hold.

decisions.decision: How should model versions be deployed and recovered?
decisions.context: Weekly device updates can introduce regressions, so deployment needs a recovery path.

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
pros: Offline operation: previous artifact can remain on device
Weekly updates: supports recovery after a bad release
cons: Tight budget: retains prior model artifacts

alternatives.label: Single model in production
pros: Tight budget: stores only the current model
cons: Weekly updates: recovery path is unspecified
Offline operation: remote recovery may be unavailable

decisions.rationale: Offline operation decides the choice: retaining a prior model allows recovery without depending on network access. This gives up device storage for previous artifacts. The design space has no source passages; this choice is grounded in d:10 and v:10.2.
consequences: Devices retain a known prior model.
Deployment tracks current and previous versions.
Rollback policy must define when to switch.

uncovered: Device update transport, synchronization, and recovery when devices reconnect.
Model and dataset artifact storage and distribution topology.
Device hardware capacity, model size, and inference latency targets.
Security and integrity checks for model artifacts.
Monitoring and reporting from intermittently connected devices.
